result.summary: Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md (all S1-S14) in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-029.md in full, then the actual diff myself (not the design doc's own claims): domain/event.ts's parseStartPayload ci_ branch, domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts's extended requireEventStaffForEvent/buildCheckinRefusalAudit, the ~340 new lines in domain/registration.ts (getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin, getCheckinActorDisplayName, getRegistrationDisplayInfo, decideQrCheckinOutcome, performQrCheckIn, decideOverrideOutcome, overrideAdmitAndCheckIn), the new handlers/checkinQr.ts in full, start.ts's dispatch addition, index.ts's callback registration, and checkinQr.db.test.ts in full (9 real-Postgres tests, confirmed not skipped by running them directly and observing 130-770ms per-test timings, not the near-instant timings a skipped DB suite would show). S5 (task item 3, my OWN non-staff-scanner scenario): traced resolveCheckinQrDeepLink (handlers/checkinQr.ts) end to end. It looks up the token first (getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin, unlocked, exists only to obtain eventId for the auth call), then calls requireEventStaffForEvent(db, tgId, lookup.eventId, lookup.eventEndsAt, now, lookup.registrationId) -- the NEW 6th parameter. Read requireEventStaffForEvent's body directly: on any !result.ok branch it calls writeAuditLog with buildCheckinRefusalAudit(user, eventId, reason, registrationId), and buildCheckinRefusalAudit's table (read directly, not assumed) maps a defined registrationId to entity:'registration'/entityId:registrationId -- not 'event'/eventId. I independently re-ran the producer's own AC1 test (checkinQr.db.test.ts, real DB, not mocked): a plain member (no EventStaff row) scans a valid admitted token via a genuine grammY /start ci_ dispatch; asserted BEFORE the scan that zero 'checkin.refused' audit rows exist for this registrationId (there is a pre-existing 'registration.admit' row from seeding, so the test correctly filters by action rather than asserting zero rows of any kind); asserted AFTER the scan exactly one 'checkin.refused' row exists with entity='registration', entityId=, actorUserId=; and that registrations.checked_in_at is still NULL. This is exactly S5's negative case ('the one case where the log matters most') and it is a real DB round-trip, not a unit-level stub. PASS. S4 (task item 4, my OWN adversarial scan): ran `git grep -n qrToken\|qr_token apps/bot/src`, excluding test files, and read every hit. qr_token is: generated once at admission (generateQrToken, REQ-020, unchanged), rendered into a deep-link PNG (domain/qr.ts, unchanged), read back only in getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin's WHERE clause (identifies ONE registration) and performQrCheckIn's locked re-read (the S4 token-currency recheck: the locked row's OWN qr_token must still equal the token supplied, or it is treated as unknown-token even though a row with that id exists -- closing the 'stale re-issued token' gap). At no point is qr_token read into any WHERE clause on `users`, never compared against any session/auth token, never used to resolve or authorize the SCANNING actor -- the scanner is always resolved via ctx.from.id -> flowUser.id (start.ts) independent of the token value. Adversarial construction: an attacker who obtains or guesses another attendee's qr_token and sends `/start ci_` is resolved as themselves (their own tgId -> their own users.id) for requireEventStaffForEvent's authorization check -- the token does not and cannot grant them EventStaff status, since checkEventStaffAuthorization never inspects the token at all, only the (eventId, resolved-actor-user.id) pair via getEventStaffRow. So a stolen token in the hands of a non-staff attacker still produces the S5-audited refusal, never a check-in, never elevated privilege. PASS. NEW-SURFACE PII CHECK (task item 5 -- 'can a non-staff scanner see ANY PII by scanning'): read resolveCheckinQrDeepLink line by line. The unlocked lookup (step 1) DOES fetch lookup.displayName/lookup.company server-side before authorization runs, but traced every branch that follows a failed authResult.ok: the 'event-ended' branch replies catalog.checkinQr.eventEnded (a fixed string, no interpolation); the 'no-user'/'not-staff-for-event' branch replies catalog.checkinQr.notStaff (also a fixed string). Neither branch references lookup.displayName, lookup.company, lookup.attendeeUserId, or any other field of `lookup` anywhere in their reply construction -- confirmed by grep for `lookup.` inside the `!authResult.ok` block: zero occurrences. The success/refusal-with-reason/already-checked-in branches that DO interpolate name/company/checked-in-actor are only reached after authResult.ok is true, i.e. only for a scanner who already passed requireEventStaffForEvent for that exact event. Independently re-ran AC5's own test (real DB, seeded real phone+email): asserts the success reply contains name+company but NOT the phone or email string -- confirms the SELECT-level exclusion (profiles.phone/profiles.email are structurally absent from getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin's select clause, confirmed by reading the query directly, not a post-fetch filter) actually holds end-to-end through a real bot dispatch. FINDING: a non-staff scanner receives ZERO PII (not even name/company) on any refusal path -- only a fixed non-personalized reply string -- because the auth-failure branches never touch the lookup object at all. AC5's phone/email exclusion is independently confirmed for the success path via the same structural-absence argument plus a real DB test. Minor observational note (not a FAIL, not filed as an issue): a non-staff scanner CAN distinguish 'unknownToken' vs 'notStaff' replies, i.e. can learn whether a given ci_ payload corresponds to SOME registration at all, without learning who. Given qr_token is a 256-bit CSPRNG value (S4, unchanged, confirmed at domain/registration.ts's generateQrToken), this is not an exploitable oracle -- the token space is not brute-forceable, and no PII beyond token-validity is disclosed by either branch. ORGANIZER-OVERRIDE AUTHORIZATION (task item 6): read makeCheckinOverrideCallbackHandler (handlers/checkinQr.ts) directly -- it calls requireOrganizerForChapter(db, tgId, event.chapterId) (domain/eventAuthorization.ts, REQ-016, confirmed absent from `git diff --name-only master...HEAD`, i.e. byte-for-byte unmodified), NEVER requireEventStaffForEvent, to gate overrideAdmitAndCheckIn. Independently re-ran the producer's own negative-case test: a real EventStaff volunteer (not organizer) taps the same override button an organizer would tap -- asserted admission stays 'withdrawn', checked_in_at stays NULL, zero 'registration.override_admit_checkin' audit rows, and the callback answer text equals catalog.checkinQr.overrideNotAuthorized. Real DB, real grammY callback dispatch. PASS. S7 CAPACITY-BYPASS SCOPING (task item 7): read decideOverrideOutcome/overrideAdmitAndCheckIn -- deliberately no capacity/seatsLeft check (correct per S7: this transition IS the explicit override S7 requires to be logged). Confirmed this bypass is NOT reachable from the ordinary QR success path: performQrCheckIn's 'check-in' branch only reaches the UPDATE when decideQrCheckinOutcome already returned 'check-in', which per its own table requires admission==='admitted' -- the UPDATE statement in that branch touches only checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method, NEVER the admission column, so it cannot re-admit or re-count anyone; the seat was already counted at the ORIGINAL admission time (registerForEvent, unchanged). The 'already-checked-in' branch performs NO write at all (verified by reading the code: it returns immediately after building the outcome object, no UPDATE call in that branch). So capacity-adjacent logic is structurally confined to overrideAdmitAndCheckIn alone -- grepped for every UPDATE...admission across the new code (2 hits: overrideAdmitAndCheckIn's UPDATE, and none in performQrCheckIn) confirming there is exactly one write path that can move a registration INTO 'admitted' outside registerForEvent's own capacity-gated flow, and it is the audited, organizer-gated one. PASS. S6 (task item 8): performQrCheckIn's UPDATE ...SET checked_in_at=$at, checked_in_by=$staffUserId, check_in_method='qr' never touches admission -- it is only reachable when the FRESH locked read (inside the same transaction) already shows admission==='admitted' (decideQrCheckinOutcome's step 2/4), so checked_in_at is set only while admission is (and remains, since this statement doesn't change it) 'admitted'. overrideAdmitAndCheckIn's UPDATE sets admission:'admitted' AND checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method in the SAME single UPDATE statement -- confirmed by reading the .set({...}) object directly: one object literal, one UPDATE call, so Postgres applies both column changes atomically within one statement; the DB CHECK constraint chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted (schema.ts, confirmed absent from the diff, i.e. unmodified) can never observe a transient state where checked_in_at is set but admission is not yet 'admitted', because there is no intermediate commit between the two column writes -- they are the same row-version write. Both paths hold SELECT...FOR UPDATE locks for the entirety of their transactions (read directly in both functions), closing REQ-028's already-established race precedent for this new code too. PASS. EVENTSTAFFAUTHORIZATION.TS BACKWARD-COMPATIBILITY (task item 9, re-derived myself, not trusted from REVIEWER): both requireEventStaffForEvent and buildCheckinRefusalAudit gained ONE new trailing OPTIONAL parameter (registrationId?: string) each. Grepped every existing call site in apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts (REQ-018/028, 3 call sites: /checkin entry, toggle callback re-auth, page-turn callback re-auth) -- all three call with exactly 5 positional arguments, omitting the new 6th parameter entirely; TypeScript optional-parameter semantics mean these calls are unchanged by the signature edit (no default-value substitution, no argument-shift risk since the new parameter is appended last, not inserted). Read buildCheckinRefusalAudit's body directly: `registrationId === undefined ? 'event'/eventId : 'registration'/registrationId` -- when omitted, produces the EXACT SAME entity/entityId pair as before this change, byte for byte. Independently re-ran the FULL suite including checkin.db.test.ts (REQ-018/028's own tests) -- all pass, confirming no behavioral regression at the only other call sites of this extended function. PASS -- the extension introduces zero new risk to already-shipped call sites. MIGRATION SIGN-OFF (S13 trigger check): `git diff master...HEAD --stat` and `git diff --name-only master...HEAD -- apps/bot/drizzle apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` both confirm ZERO migration files and ZERO schema.ts changes in this diff -- verified by direct diff, not by trusting the design doc's 'Schema: NO CHANGE' claim. S13's migration-sign-off duty does not trigger; N/A, not silently skipped. REMAINING S1-S14 ITEMS: - S1: N/A -- no consent-column write anywhere in this diff (grepped consent_pd_at/broadcast_opt_in/publish_consent across every changed file -- zero hits); the design's own 'why no consent gate' reasoning (§1.2) is sound and consistent with REQ-018/020/028's existing precedent of never consent-gating a staff/organizer actor's own action. - S2: PASS -- covered under 'organizer-override authorization' and S4/S5 above; EventStaff gate is per-event (unchanged getEventStaffRow predicate), organizer gate is per-chapter (unchanged requireOrganizerForChapter), neither is conflated with the other in this diff. - S3: PASS -- covered under 'new-surface PII check' above; no non-staff scanner and no staff scanner of a DIFFERENT event's registration can reach this flow at all (requireEventStaffForEvent is keyed to lookup.eventId, itself derived from the SCANNED token, so there is no cross-event angle distinct from S4/S5's own token-scoping). - S6: PASS (above). - S7: PASS (above). - S8: PASS -- performQrCheckIn's check-in branch: exactly one UPDATE + one writeAuditLog, same tx; overrideAdmitAndCheckIn: exactly one UPDATE + one writeAuditLog, same tx; already-checked-in and refused-not-admitted branches: zero writes, zero audit rows (reporting existing state is not a status change). Grepped 'registration.checkin'/'registration.override_admit_checkin' across apps/bot/src -- each action string's writeAuditLog call site appears exactly once. - S9/S10: N/A -- no notification/broadcast send introduced by this diff. - S11: PASS -- grepped for console./log. calls across the full diff (zero matches); every new writeAuditLog payload contains only { eventId }, { eventId, method }, { eventId, previousAdmission }, or { reason } -- no phone/email/name/tgUsername in any payload. - S12: N/A -- no export functionality touched. - S13: N/A, trigger not met (see Migration sign-off above). - S14: N/A -- no Profile/publish_consent code touched. COMMANDS RUN BY ME, REAL OUTPUT: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx/Nav.tsx, outside apps/bot). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces (Next.js + bot tsc) clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 28 files / 286 tests passed, 0 failed (up from REQ-028's 26/272, consistent with this diff's one new test file). `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.db.test.ts --reporter=verbose` alone -> 9/9 passed, each test 130-770ms (real Postgres round-trips, not a skipped suite). Scope/hygiene: `git status --short` clean before my review; no files modified by me other than this handoff. Verdict: PASS. S5's audit-on-non-staff-refusal now correctly names entity=registration/entityId= (independently reproduced against a real DB); S4's token-currency recheck closes the stale-token gap and the token is never usable to authorize the scanning actor under any adversarial construction I could build; the override's authorization is genuinely the stricter organizer-scoped gate, not the staff gate; S7's capacity bypass is structurally confined to the one audited override path; S6 holds by single-statement atomicity in both write paths; the eventStaffAuthorization.ts extension is a true no-op for every pre-existing call site. No blocking defect found across S1-S14.

commands: git diff master...HEAD --stat -> confirms scope (event.ts, eventStaffAuthorization.ts, registration.ts, checkinQr.ts new, checkinQr.db.test.ts new, start.ts, i18n x3, index.ts, design doc, handoffs) and zero migration/schema.ts files
git grep -n 'qrToken\|qr_token' apps/bot/src (excluding tests) -> every hit read directly; token never used to resolve/authorize the scanning actor, only to identify one registration
grep -n requireEventStaffForEvent apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts -> 3 call sites, all with exactly 5 args (new 6th param omitted, backward-compatible)
npm run lint (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors

npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root) -> 28 files / 286 tests passed, 0 failed
npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.db.test.ts --reporter=verbose -> 9/9 passed, 130-770ms each (real Postgres, not skipped)
evidence.s5_negative_case: Non-EventStaff member scans a valid admitted token via a real /start ci_<token> grammY dispatch (real DB test, independently re-run by me): exactly one 'checkin.refused' audit row is written, with entity='registration', entityId=<the exact registrationId>, actorUserId=<the non-staff scanner's own users.id>; no check-in write occurs; the reply is a fixed non-personalized notStaff string carrying no PII.
evidence.s4_adversarial_case: An attacker holding a stolen/guessed qr_token still authenticates as THEMSELVES via ctx.from.id (never via the token) when calling requireEventStaffForEvent; checkEventStaffAuthorization's predicate never inspects the token, only the (eventId, resolved-actor-user.id) EventStaff pair, so a stolen token cannot grant EventStaff status or check-in privilege to a non-staff holder -- it only ever identifies which registration would be affected IF the scanner is separately authorized.
evidence.non_staff_pii_finding: Zero PII (not even name/company) is disclosed to a non-staff scanner on any refusal path -- the !authResult.ok branch's replies (eventEnded, notStaff) are fixed strings that never reference the pre-authorization lookup object. Minor observational, non-blocking note: a non-staff scanner can distinguish 'token exists' (notStaff) from 'token unknown' (unknownToken) without seeing WHO the token belongs to; not exploitable given the token's 256-bit CSPRNG entropy (S4, unchanged) and not filed as an issue.
evidence.override_authorization_case: requireOrganizerForChapter (REQ-016, confirmed byte-for-byte unmodified) gates overrideAdmitAndCheckIn, never requireEventStaffForEvent. Independently re-ran the producer's negative-case test: a real EventStaff volunteer (not organizer) tapping the override button is refused (overrideNotAuthorized), zero writes, zero override audit rows -- real DB, real callback dispatch.
evidence.s7_scoping: performQrCheckIn's UPDATE never touches the admission column (only checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method) and is only reachable when admission is already 'admitted'; the already-checked-in branch performs no write at all. The only UPDATE...admission='admitted' outside registerForEvent's capacity-gated flow is overrideAdmitAndCheckIn's single, organizer-gated, audited UPDATE.
evidence.s6_atomicity: overrideAdmitAndCheckIn sets admission:'admitted' and checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method in one .set({...}) object, i.e. one UPDATE statement -- no transient state where checked_in_at is set without admission='admitted' can exist for the CHECK constraint to observe.
evidence.backward_compat_recheck: buildCheckinRefusalAudit's registrationId===undefined branch reproduces the exact pre-existing entity:'event'/entityId:eventId pair; all 3 REQ-018/028 call sites omit the new parameter; full suite (including checkin.db.test.ts) passes unchanged.
